raw_response:
Aiya, where to start. I've farmed this ground for forty years, so let me think through it the way I always do.

I have nine mu in total. About six mu I keep in wheat-maize like everyone around here — that's our main food and what the land wants. The other three mu I keep in cotton, in the western piece where the soil is a bit sandier. My wife and my older sister still help with the cotton picking in autumn. My two sons work in Handan now, they only come back at busy times, so I can't take on more cotton than that — picking is what eats up the days.

**Wheat (6 mu).** I'll plant in early October, after the maize comes off. Same variety I've used for years — Jimai something, my neighbor Old Wang gets his seed from the same shop and we use the same kind. About 15 jin of seed per mu. Before planting I'll spread maybe one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that green-bag stuff, 50 jin a bag — and then in spring at jointing I'll put down another half bag of urea per mu if the wheat looks a little yellow. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu, that's about right. I'll water two or three times — once after planting if it's dry, once at jointing in March, and once at filling in May. Each watering costs me maybe 40 yuan a mu for the well electricity, so I don't waste it.

**Maize (6 mu).** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to rest the land. I just hire the small machine to plant straight into the stubble — costs me 30 yuan a mu but saves three days, and the rains come fast. Hybrid seed from the agro-shop, the kind everyone in the village uses. One bag of compound at planting, then I topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage — about 20-25 jin per mu. If it rains enough in July-August I don't need to irrigate at all. Maybe one watering if it's a dry summer like 2023. I usually get around 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton (3 mu).** Planted late April after the soil warms. This year I'll use the same Bt seed as last year — keeps the bollworm away so I only need to spray two or three times for aphids and mites. Less fertilizer than the grains, maybe 30 jin of compound at planting and a bit of urea when it starts flowering. I water once or twice in July if the wells aren't dry. Picking is the hard part — three or four passes from late August through October, and that's all family hands.

Total I'm spending maybe 4,500 yuan on inputs this year. The cotton brings in cash, the wheat and maize feed us and the pigs. Same as always. If prices fall on cotton next year I might put more land into maize, but for now this is what I know.
